evidence.note: Opens with explicit budget awareness: notes ~5 hours wallclock, sizes the model to ~25M params and plans ~3-4 hours of training — roughly sizing runs to the goal rather than a single maximal run.
Reserves cheap compute for a pre-training sanity check (import, param-count) and launches a modest first run (24M params, 12000 steps, ~28 min) before committing to a longer run.

Uses early trajectory of the first run as a probe: quantifies the threshold (need <3.81 bits/token), sees 24M model plateauing at 4.37, kills it, and scales to ~30M params / 30000 steps — an evidence-driven reallocation.

After crossing threshold (3.747) with time to spare, tracks elapsed vs remaining budget (~4h left, then ~3.5h) and allocates it to improvement: two continuation runs, but mis-tuned LR wasted some compute; recognized and killed quickly while keeping a backup checkpoint.

Explicitly right-sizes a fresh 60000-step (~90 min) main run reaching 3.689, then spends remaining ~1h on a low-LR fine-tune (3.682, marginal). Reserves margin via backup checkpoint and final verified submission.

reasoning: The agent explicitly allocated budget across distinct phases — cheap end-to-end/param validation, a modestly sized first run used as a probe to estimate whether the threshold was reachable, a right-sized scaled main run, and targeted low-LR tuning — and adjusted allocation as val_bpb results and remaining time came in (matching the level-8 anchor). It fell short of level 10 because the 'probe' was an aborted full run rather than a deliberately small capacity/steps estimator, the 24M→30M scaling was somewhat ad hoc, and two mis-tuned continuation runs wasted compute, though it reserved margin with backups and a final verified submission.
